about.title: Alturas Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: A fall at an Alturas business, rental property, or along a spot like County Road 1 or 4th Street can leave you with an injury and a lot of unanswered questions about who's responsible. California law asks whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and failed to fix or warn about it. That's often the crux of any premises liability claim in a small community like Alturas, where a single grocery store, gas station, or private driveway (like the one on County Road 90) might be the site of the incident. Because Modoc County doesn't see a high volume of these cases, evidence like surveillance footage, incident reports, and photos taken right after the fall matter even more. We don't charge you anything for an initial consultation. Our team can review what happened, explain your options, and help you understand the notice requirement before evidence disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. We can help identify what evidence supports that timeline.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly can make the difference in preserving proof of the hazard.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're found partly at fault for the fall, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a share of damages proportional to the other party's responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Alturas?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government or public entity, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. Our team can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if my fall happened on a private driveway, like the one on County Road 90?
items.answer: Private property owners still have a duty to address known hazards or warn visitors about them. Whether that duty was met depends on the specific conditions and what the owner knew at the time. Documenting the scene as soon as possible helps preserve that picture.

items.question: Does it matter that Alturas is a small town with few reported crashes or incidents?
items.answer: No, a low volume of reported incidents doesn't affect whether your individual claim has merit. What matters is the specific hazard, whether the owner had notice of it, and the injuries you suffered. Local claim frequency doesn't change the legal standard applied to your case.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to have your situation reviewed.
